components.name: Gradient Ring Button
components.description: The site's signature pill button: a gradient ring around a dark fill, inverting on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { position: relative; display: inline-block; z-index: 30; border-radius: 50px; padding: 1vw; font-size: 36px; color: #DDDDDD; border: none; background: transparent; transition: color 1s ease-in; } .ds-btn-primary::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -2px; left: -2px; right: -2px; bottom: -2px; border-radius: inherit; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #DA107B, #01ECF3); z-index: -2; transition: background 1s ease-in; } .ds-btn-primary::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 100%; height: 100%; top: 0; left: 0; border-radius: inherit; background: #001412; padding: 2px; box-sizing: border-box; z-index: -1; transition: background 1s ease-in; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { color: #222222; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover::before { background: #222222; } .ds-btn-primary:hover::after { background: linear-gradient(150deg, #DA107B, #01ECF3); }

components.name: Gradient Ring Card
components.description: Project card: gradient-ring border around a dark fill, title + scrollable description + pill link.
components.html: Project TitleShort project description goes here, scrolls if it overflows the fixed card height.Presentation
components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 350px; height: 225px; padding: 20px; margin: 25px; border-radius: 15px; z-index: 30; } .ds-card::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -2px; left: -2px; right: -2px; bottom: -2px; border-radius: inherit; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #DA107B, #01ECF3); z-index: -2; } .ds-card::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 100%; height: 100%; top: 0; left: 0; border-radius: inherit; background: #001412; padding: 2px; box-sizing: border-box; z-index: -1; } .ds-card-title { display: block; color: #EEEEEE; font-size: clamp(19px, 2vw, 25px); margin-bottom: 1vw; } .ds-card-desc { display: block; flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; color: #EEEEEE; font-weight: 300; font-size: 18px; text-align: left; padding-right: 20px; scrollbar-color: #DA107B transparent; scrollbar-width: thin; } .ds-card-link { align-self: flex-start; margin-top: auto; color: #fff; font-size: 22px; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; border: #eee solid 1px; border-radius: 50px; padding: 7px 15px; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #DA107B, #01ECF3); transition: all 0.5s; } .ds-card-link:hover { color: #000; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #01ECF3, #DA107B, #01ECF3); }

components.name: Gradient Ring Input
components.description: Pill text input wrapped in the gradient-ring container, transparent fill, no literal border.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; display: inline-block; margin: 20px; border-radius: 50px; background-color: #001412; z-index: 30; } .ds-input-wrap::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -2px; left: -2px; right: -2px; bottom: -2px; border-radius: inherit; background: linear-gradient(150deg, #DA107B, #01ECF3); z-index: -2; } .ds-input-wrap::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 100%; height: 100%; top: 0; left: 0; border-radius: inherit; background: #001412; padding: 2px; box-sizing: border-box; z-index: -1; } .ds-input { border: none; background-color: transparent; position: relative; display: inline-block; font-size: 24px; color: #DDDDDD; width: 17vw; padding: 10px; font-family: 'Inconsolata', monospace; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; }

narrative.overview:
A single-page dark portfolio built around one recurring device: a magenta-to-cyan gradient that never fills a surface, only traces its edge. Every interactive container — buttons, cards, inputs — sits on the same near-black teal fill (#001412) and gets its identity from a thin glowing ring rather than a flat color block or a drop shadow. Behind the hero and section headers, the same two hues reappear as huge, heavily blurred blooms, standing in for shadows and giving the page its ambient, backlit feel.

The system is not a formal, exhaustively-tokenized design system — it's a hand-built personal site with one strong, consistently-applied idea. Titles are set in a custom stencil display face (AllertaStencil); everything else runs in a monospace body face (Inconsolata), giving the whole thing a "technical/dev" voice appropriate for a software engineer's CV.
keyCharacteristics: One background: near-black teal (#001412), everywhere, no light surfaces.
One accent system: the magenta↔cyan gradient, used as a border/bloom, never a fill.
Depth from light (blur blooms), not shadow.
Every corner is either a full pill (buttons, inputs) or a soft 15px rectangle (cards) — nothing sharp.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Law
rules.body: All structural color comes from the magenta↔cyan gradient and its tonal siblings. Red/green/deeppink/blueviolet are reserved for isolated functional signals and never appear in navigation, cards, or buttons.

rules.name: The Stencil-For-Structure Rule
rules.body: AllertaStencil is reserved for section/identity titles only (name, section headers, card titles). Body copy, buttons, and form fields stay in Inconsolata.

rules.name: The Bloom-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth cues are large blurred gradient blooms behind content, never box-shadow on the content itself.

dos: Do build any new bordered container with the Gradient Ring technique (::before gradient inset -2px at z-index -2, ::after Void Teal fill at z-index -1) instead of a literal border.
Do keep every surface on Void Teal (#001412); this system has no light/white surface.
Do use blurred, low-opacity gradient blooms for depth behind hero or section content, sized generously (blur(70-130px), opacity 0.6).
Do set section/identity titles in AllertaStencil and leave body copy in Inconsolata.
Do size type and spacing with clamp()/vw so new sections scale fluidly rather than snapping at fixed breakpoints.
donts: Don't introduce box-shadow as a default depth cue — the flip-card is the one accepted exception, not a pattern to extend.
Don't use square or sharp corners; every surface is pill (50px) or soft-rect (15px/10px).
Don't bring a third structural hue into buttons, cards, or nav — red/green/deeppink/blueviolet stay confined to their one existing functional signal each.
